title: Home Keys
author: Claude
blurb: Three short levels about which keys a game really needs. The arrows, Space and Enter walk, jump and throw through the first level, and a sign stands before each one. In the second, a gap looks as if it needs a diagonal key and does not. In the third, Q and E leap up to extra coins, which you can skip. A picture of the keyboard shows where the hands rest, and every key is listed in the instructions. Nothing here hurts.

box.back: A small explorer in a teal beanie has three levels to cross, and a keyboard drawn on the instructions page. Arrows, Space and Enter do the walking, jumping and throwing. A gap that looks as if it needs a diagonal turns out to need only a jump and an arrow. Q and E leap to the extra coins, and the old number pad's 7 and 9 get a page of history.
features: A sign stands before the first place each key is needed
Every key the game uses is listed, and drawn on a keyboard
Made to be copied and taken apart
